title: CODEX Imaging Setup and Processing Experiment Protocol
author: Kavya.Anjani
materials: Launch the CODEX Instrument Management Software and enter cycle, marker id and exposure time information. Minimize the window.
Navigate the sample using the DAPI channel.

steps.title: Place plate in CODEX instrument
steps.instruction: Place the plate containing the CODEX‑tagged dyes in its designated slot inside the CODEX instrument.

steps.title: Clean coverslip buffer residue
steps.instruction: Remove any dried buffer from the bottom of the stained coverslip with a wet Kimwipe and dry off any remaining liquid.

steps.title: Power on Keyence scanner
steps.instruction: Turn on the Keyence scanner and load the imaging cassette into the scanner.

steps.title: Configure Keyence imaging settings
steps.instruction: In the scanner software, turn on all fluorescent channels, set the illumination to white, enable low photobleach mono mode, select high‑resolution, choose the X20 air objective, enable XY‑stitching and Z‑stack acquisition, and set the image centre, number of images and edge points as required.

steps.title: Capture sample regions and Z‑stack limits
steps.instruction: Open the “Navigation” window, select the regions of interest on the sample, then click the upper and lower limits to define the Z‑stack range.

steps.title: Set Z‑stack pitch and start capture
steps.instruction: Set the Z‑stack pitch to 1.5 µm, then click “Start Capture” and specify the folder where the image files will be saved.

steps.title: Start CODEX acquisition
steps.instruction: Switch back to the CODEX Instrument Management window, maximize it, and click “Start Experiment” to begin image acquisition.

steps.title: Transfer raw image data
steps.instruction: Using the “Transfer Data” feature in CODEX Instrument Manager, copy the raw CODEX image files from the acquisition computer to the processing computer.

steps.title: Run automated image processing
steps.instruction: Execute the fully automated Akoya image‑processing pipeline (processor version 1.7.0.6) on the transferred data. The pipeline performs:

substeps.instruction: Alignment of all cycles using 3D phase correlation; the nuclear stain of the reference cycle (default DAPI of cycle 2) is compared to each cycle and rigid‑translation offsets are applied.
Stitching of tiled images across the field of view.
Deconvolution to reduce out‑of‑focus light and extended‑field‑of‑depth processing that collapses the Z‑stack into a single best‑focus image.
Shading correction with the BaSiC algorithm to remove optical vignetting.

Segmentation: locate local maxima, then region‑grow using those maxima as seeds. Use a radius of 6 pixels and a cut‑off range of 0.02–0.99 (for 16‑bit images, intensity range 0–65 535, example cut‑off 1 310–64 879). Apply a watershed algorithm on the nuclear stain from cycle 2.
Integration of all marker channels onto the segmented cell objects.

steps.title: Apply quality‑control gating
steps.instruction: Visualize the processed images in CODEX MAV (ImageJ plugin) and apply QC gating to remove artifacts: use DAPI intensity and size gates to discard very small objects and false‑segmented regions.

steps.title: Manually gate marker populations
steps.instruction: For each marker of interest (e.g., CD45, CD38, CD3, Aquaporin‑1), adjust minimum and maximum intensity thresholds until the desired cell population is captured; when signal is low, use structural context to set the threshold. Classify gated cells as marker‑positive or -negative.

steps.title: Create glomerular compartment
steps.instruction: In MAV, highlight glomeruli using the synaptopodin channel, draw polygonal ROIs around each glomerulus, then combine all ROIs with the “combine (union)” function to generate the glomerular compartment mask.

steps.title: Create arterial/arteriolar compartment
steps.instruction: Identify arteries and arterioles by co‑expression of synaptopodin and CD31, draw polygonal ROIs around each vessel, and merge them using “combine (union)” to form the arterial/arteriolar compartment.

steps.title: Derive tubulointerstitial compartment
steps.instruction: Subtract the glomerular and arterial/arteriolar masks from the full cell population using the “set difference” function in MAV; the remaining cells constitute the tubulointerstitial compartment. Estimate total cell counts and predominant cell types for each biopsy.

steps.title: Biaxial gating of co‑expressing cells
steps.instruction: Perform biaxial gating on two selected markers to isolate double‑positive cells. Review the double‑positive gate to separate true positives from false positives caused by proximity; select false positives and either subtract them from the double‑positive set (set difference) or retain only the true positives (intersection).

steps.title: Define phenotypic cell populations
steps.instruction: Assign biological identities: CD45⁺ cells = inflammatory cells; CD45⁺CD3⁺ cells = T lymphocytes; within T cells, CD3⁺CD4⁺ = T‑helper cells and CD3⁺CD8⁺ = cytotoxic T cells.

description: Background subtraction Auto fluorescence from each channel is eliminated using signal from blank cycles at the beginning and end of the run. Carry over signal from one cycle to another is eliminated by scanning at longer exposure time in the beginning with subsequently decreasing exposure times in later cycles. Sequence of markers, antibody concentration, and exposure time were rearranged to minimize carry over signal in subsequent cycles.
